gmm.support: very strong support for two groups
gmm.verdict: ΔBIC = +993.2 (one group 24566.2, two groups 23573.0): very strong support for two groups. BIC compares Gaussian shapes, and a single skewed cloud can earn two components, so this is evidence, not proof. But its two groups are barely the DS / P-spike split (adjusted Rand 0.06, where 1 is the same split and 0 is chance; 63% of events the same): two Gaussians fit the cloud's SHAPE better than one, which a single skewed spectrum also does. Read the split-axis histogram before reading this as two populations.

dbic_scale: very strong support for two groups

measure.filter_label: custom filter, 10–150 Hz, 60 Hz mains out

rule: Pooled over 9 recordings from 9 mice, in pooled raw units: the cluster whose centre has more 240–420 Hz power is called P-spike: +22.5 dB against +12.0 dB for the other, which is called DS (1832 DS, 1185 P-spike, 1 not measured).

scale.why: Pooled raw units, z-scored once across the pool: differences in size between mice stay visible, impedance and placement included.

split_axis.unit: z, 0 at the midpoint, DS negative
